subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram inline buttons for pairing approve/deny

question: Should Telegram-originated inline-button callbacks be allowed to approve or deny pairing and device requests, and which scopes may they satisfy for DM pairing versus `operator.admin` browser/device approvals?
rationale: The requested UX moves access-changing approval from CLI or scoped gateway clients into Telegram callback handling, and current source intentionally limits Telegram command-owner approval scope to `operator.pairing`.

options.title: Design typed approval actions
options.body: Define reusable approval actions with request id, action, expiry, single-use semantics, caller identity, audit, and existing scope enforcement before rendering Telegram buttons.

options.title: Limit first pass to DM pairing
options.body: Add buttons only for low-scope channel DM pairing and keep `operator.admin` browser/device approvals on CLI or Control UI until a separate step-up model lands.

options.title: Defer chat-originated approvals
options.body: Keep the command-copy workflow until the broader channel-aware device approval and step-up authorization direction is settled.

recommendation.title: Design typed approval actions
recommendation.body: Define reusable approval actions with request id, action, expiry, single-use semantics, caller identity, audit, and existing scope enforcement before rendering Telegram buttons.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the broadest recent history across pairing messages, device-pair notify state, pairing routes, and adjacent approval/security docs.
